title: Vote counts in Alaska, Mississippi and Kansas continue after Democratic sweep
text:
Vote counts in Alaska, Mississippi and Kansas continue after Democratic sweep 
 EVENT ENDED Last updated November 05, 2026, 10:08 PM EST Vote counts in Alaska, Mississippi and Kansas continue after Democratic sweep
 Nithya Raman, a democratic socialist, will be the next mayor of Los Angeles, NBC News projects.
 'Blue arrows everywhere': How Trump's 2024 coalition shifted in 2026 03:59 
 Save Add NBC News to Google Updated November 05, 2026, 10:08 PM EST By NBC News What to know today 
 LOS ANGELES MAYOR: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman has defeated incumbent Karen Bass, NBC News projects, capping a rapid political ascent for a progressive challenger who railed against the “broken status quo” in the country’s second-largest metropolis.
 UNCALLED RACES: In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola is leading GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan by around 600 votes, and in Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom is leading GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 1,800 votes. There are 30 uncalled races in the House, where the NBC News Decision Desk estimates Democrats will control at least 259 seats in the next Congress.
 KANSAS GOVERNOR: The race for governor in Kansas is also too close to call, with Democrat Cindy Holscher leading Republican Ty Masterson by several thousand votes out of the million-plus cast.
 DOJ DEPARTURE: Harmeet Dhillon, the Republican attorney who oversaw a massive overhaul of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, submitted her resignation today, two days after Democrats won majorities in both houses of Congress in the midterm elections.
 Coverage of this live blog has ended. For the latest news, click here. 
 NEW UPDATES 2d ago / 10:08 PM EST A district-level look at the huge shifts across the House battlefield 
 The most competitive House districts in the country shifted to the left dramatically, with Democrats running up the score in key races and racking up impressive wins in red districts, according to an analysis of the House races NBC News’ Decision Desk rated as “battleground districts” before the election.
 The average battleground district’s margin moved almost 16 percentage points toward Democrats compared with the 2024 presidential margin there, according to a review of the election results in 20 of the 28 battlegrounds where at least 95% of the expected vote is in.
 Read the full story here. 
 2d ago / 9:19 PM EST Many Republicans leaned into the ‘culture wars’ on the campaign trail. It didn’t work. 
 Gina Hinojosa barnstormed across Texas in her successful campaign for governor, speaking to legions of voters anxious about stubborn inflation, high gas prices and more. But there was one topic that the 52-year-old Democrat ruled off-limits.
 “We’re not doing the culture wars,” Hinojosa told an interviewer in late September. “We are talking about how we’re gonna deliver for Texans, how we’re gonna make life easier for working families.” When it came to divisive social issues such as abortion access and transgender rights, she said, her campaign would “not take the bait.”
 It was a blunt expression of a winning strategy that Democrats followed across the country on their way to sweeping victories in Congress and a majority of the country’s gubernatorial seats — and a sharp contrast with some Republican candidates and groups that spent heavily trying to make transgender rights and other social issues central to the midterms.
 Read the full story here. 
 2d ago / 9:01 PM EST Nithya Raman expresses gratitude for Karen Bass, says their teams are in touch about Los Angeles mayoral transition 
 City Council member Nithya Raman today expressed her "deepest gratitude" for Mayor Karen Bass and her "decades of service to the city" following her projected victory in the Los Angeles mayor's race.
 Raman said she spoke with Bass this morning and applauded her for making the city a "deeply inclusive place."
 "This city has opened its arms to people to come and build their dreams here, and the idea that Angelenos voted for an immigrant to be their next mayor at this moment in American history is so deeply moving to me," she said in celebratory remarks with staffers at the Original Farmers Market in Los Angeles.
 Raman said that most of her day has been taken up by congratulatory calls but that her staff and Bass' are in touch to ensure the mayoral administration handoff is "the smoothest possible transition."
 "We have 40 days to build this transition," she said. "It’s one of the shortest transitions across the country for a city of 4 million people, where the challenges are absolutely immense. That transition is going to be absolutely critical."
 2d ago / 8:57 PM EST Rep. Ro Khanna says he is 'thinking' about a 2028 presidential bid 
 Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., said today that he is thinking about running for president in 2028.
 “Yes, I’m thinking about it,” Khanna said on MS NOW when he was asked about NBC News’ reporting that his allies are trying to draft him to make a bid.
 “There are a lot of great candidates in the party and people who have different ideas. And I think it’s going to be wonderful, cathartic for this country. After three 80-year-old presidents, we’re finally going to get a new generation on both parties offering a vision of how to move America forward,” he added.
 Khanna, who said in a statement responding to the draft committee that he would make a decision with his family after the holidays, has previously said he’s considering a bid. He told NPR in August, before the blue surge that swept the midterms this week, that he was “seriously” thinking about running.
 2d ago / 8:51 PM EST Arizona rejects Proposition 144: Require voter ID and citizenship to vote, NBC News projects 
 Arizona voters have rejected Proposition 144: Require voter ID and citizenship to vote, NBC News projects.
 See the latest results here. 
 2d ago / 7:56 PM EST Newly elected Democrats could become 2028 presidential power brokers 
 The 2026 midterm elections are not quite over, but the 2028 presidential race may soon get underway.
 And with sweeping victories for Democrats in races across the country Tuesday night, voters in states with early Democratic presidential primaries also elected a new class of kingmakers.
 Read the full story here. 
 2d ago / 7:31 PM EST Trump repeats insistence that Republicans would have won if he were on the ballot 
 Two days after the midterm elections, Trump continues to blame the GOP’s losses on his absence from the ballot, despite having repeatedly told Republicans over the past few months to vote as if he were on it .
 “I JUST WASN’T ON THE BALLOT. IF I WERE, WE WOULD HAVE WON IN A LANDSLIDE!” Trump wrote on Truth Social tonight.
 Trump made the same argument on election night after it became clear that Democrats were on their way to taking control of Congress. On that night, he told several news outlets in phone interviews that his not appearing on the ballot was the reason for the Republican losses. Exit polling suggests otherwise .
 On the campaign trail, Trump told voters to “pretend” like he was on the ballot, and he often said, “In many ways, I am.”
 2d ago / 7:14 PM EST Democrats’ midterm win threatens to disrupt Trump’s fragile truce with Xi 
 Almost two years after Trump returned to office, Washington’s rocky relationship with Beijing has found steadier footing, based largely on what observers say is his personal rapport with Chinese leader Xi Jinping . But U.S.-China relations could be injected with new volatility as control of Congress shifts to Democrats who might press for tougher stances on Taiwan , AI and other issues.
 The Democrats’ sweeping victory in this week’s U.S. midterm elections comes two weeks before Trump is set to meet Xi in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, their third in-person meeting this year.
 Read the full story here. 
 Andrew Harnik / Getty 
 2d ago / 6:37 PM EST Colorado approves Proposition 134: Biological sex requirement for school sports, NBC News projects 
 Colorado voters have approved Proposition 134: Biological sex requirement for school sports, NBC News projects.
 See the latest results here. 
 2d ago / 6:35 PM EST Trump reacts to major market sell-off: 'It wasn’t Republicans' 
 Trump took notice of today's sharp market sell-off and weighed in on Truth Social .
 "The Stock Market suffered one of the Worst Days in History based on the results of the Election. Such a sad thing to watch!" he wrote.
 Earlier in the day, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite stock indexes plummeted in their worst one-day drops since April 2025, when the rollout of Trump's tariffs sent markets plummeting. Tech stocks today collectively lost more than $2 trillion in value.
 Still, the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 are still up by nearly 30% since Election Day 2024.
 Show more In his post, Trump added: “It took so much work to get us to a level that no one has ever seen before, and then this. Your 401(k)s have, therefore, dropped. Remember, it wasn’t Republicans, it was Dumocrats. Do not fear, however, we will soon, one way or the other, be BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE.”
 However, it was the change from Republican majority control of the House, the Senate and numerous governorships that rocked markets. With many Democratic lawmakers now preparing to take office, many of whom have backed data center construction slowdowns or halts, investors dumped stocks linked to the sector, worried that trillions of dollars of investments may not eventually pay off.
 2d ago / 6:29 PM EST Trump seeks to prevent significant changes to the Oval Office and Cabinet Room by designating them as national monuments 
 Trump signed a proclamation today to designate the Oval Office and the Cabinet Room as official federal landmarks, a move he said was designed to ensure no significant changes are made to them in the future.
 “We’re going to be declaring it a national monument, and we're going to send it over to Congress to have it ratified," Trump told reporters this afternoon in the Oval Office. "It won’t be able to be taken down, destroyed, touched or anything else."
 Jim Lo Scalzo / Bloomberg via Getty 
 The White House has been officially designated as a U.S. National Historic Landmark since 1960, though the order Trump signed today said "the Oval Office merits specific recognition and protective management as a discrete historic structure of national significance."
 Trump said he felt it was "very important that nobody be allowed to come in and take it down and try and do something with it." He said "major modifications" to the room would have to be approved by Congress, adding that he hopes "the people in Congress will be smart enough not to let that happen."
 Show more Trump faced backlash over his decision to demolish the historic East Wing to build his new White House ballroom.
 It is common for new presidents to change furniture and artwork and make other design choices in the Oval Office at the starts of their terms. When Trump returned to office in 2025, he completely redecorated the Oval Office, filling it with his signature favorite: lots and lots of gold.
 Andrew Harnik / Getty 
 Today's proclamation says future presidents would still be able to "redecorate the monument, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security modifications" as long as they do not "substantially impair the monument’s historic structure or architectural character."
 In discussing the proclamation, Trump emphasized the “victories” he has achieved in the Oval Office, adding, “I mean, there’s been some mistakes, too.” He did not elaborate.
 3d ago / 6:15 PM EST Democrat Cait Conley wins New York's 17th Congressional District, NBC News projects 
 Democrat Cait Conley has defeated Republican Mike Lawler to win New York's 17th Congressional District, NBC News projects.
 See the latest results here. 
 3d ago / 6:10 PM EST Mississippi Republican Party chair pledges every vote will be counted in tight Senate race 
 Mississippi Republican Party Chair Mike Hurst pledged at a news conference today that every vote will be counted as Republicans scramble to make sure GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith wins re-election in a surprisingly tight race against Democrat Scott Colom.
 He boasted that Republicans “have built an incredible election integrity program for exact moments like this" and that the state party had 50 volunteer attorneys and observers deployed across the state who are focused on the Senate race. Hurst said they estimate 20,000 ballots are left to be counted.
 Azariah Wells / Jackson State University via Getty 
 “This is what the Mississippi Republican Party and the RNC has spent years building, an operation ready before the fight begins and prepared to fight until it ends. Every outstanding ballot, every county, every deadline, every legal option will get our full attention. We will not sleep until we know that our elections are secure,” he said.
 Show more “We are firm in our conviction that if the law is and was followed that Mississippians will have spoken clearly and unequivocally and that Sen. Hyde Smith will be re-elected to another term to represent the great state of Mississippi,” he added.
 An NBC News reporter pressed Hurst about his insistence that Hyde-Smith would win if every ballot is fairly counted and the law is followed.
 “Listen, I’m always willing to accept a scenario where the voters have spoken and the law has been followed," Hurst said. "Let me be clear: There is no election-denying going on here. If the laws are followed and the voters spoke, that is it. And Mississippi Republicans will accept that."
 3d ago / 5:51 PM EST The Justice Department is investigating the 2022 Supreme Court leak 
 The Justice Department is investigating the leak of information from the Supreme Court related to its 2022 decision that overturned abortion rights, two sources familiar with the investigation said today.
 The Supreme Court previously conducted its own internal review of the leak , which led to a Politico report on the Dobbs vs. Jackson Women’s Health Organization draft decision before it ruling was issued.
 The New York Times first reported on the Justice Department's involvement in investigating the leak.
 The Justice Department declined to comment, and the Office of the U.S. attorney for D.C., Jeanine Pirro, responded with “no comment.”
 The scope of the review, including potential targets and specific violations, was not immediately clear. 
 3d ago / 5:42 PM EST Pete Hegseth says any effort to impeach him won't work 
 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth struck a defiant tone today responding to Kentucky GOP Rep. Thomas Massie’s plans to introduce impeachment articles against him.
 Brendan Smialowski / AFP via Getty 
 Four minutes into a five-minute video on X , Hegseth alluded to Massie without mentioning him by name.
 “A disgruntled, defeated congressman, along with all his Democrat allies, has also dropped sham articles of impeachment against yours truly, just like they tried against President Trump twice,” Hegseth said.
 “It’s all about the politics of personal destruction. Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me. You can rest assured of that,” he added.
 Trump said yesterday that he is not planning to replace Hegseth, adding today that “he has done a fantastic job” and “probably has opposition” over the actions he’s taken, including purging military leadership.
 Show more Massie said last night on social media that the “only contingency” in which he would not introduce articles of impeachment against Hegseth was if he resigned. Massie is set to leave Congress in January after he lost his primary to a Trump-backed challenger.
 3d ago / 5:19 PM EST Anticipation, optimism take hold as Mississippi’s Senate race becomes a nail-biter 
 The last time Mississippi sent a Democratic senator to Washington, college students casting their first votes this week hadn’t even been born. And 1982 was long enough ago that there’s a good chance some of their professors hadn’t, either.
 The race between the Republican incumbent, Cindy Hyde-Smith, the first woman to serve in the role, and Scott Colom, a Democrat who would be the state’s first Black senator since Reconstruction, is still too close to call. Yet, from the halls of a Masonic Lodge in Jackson, once walked by Civil Rights-era leaders , to the grounds of a nearby historically Black university, there was a feeling yesterday that the state was on the cusp of a new chapter.
 Read the full story here. 
 Brad Vest / Getty 
 3d ago / 4:38 PM EST NAACP deploys more staff to Mississippi as tight Senate race remains uncalled 
 The NAACP said today that it has deployed national staff members and other resources to Mississippi as the Senate race there remains too close to call, with Democrat Scott Colom leading GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by less than 2,000 votes.
 Democrat Scott Colom and Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss.   Imagn; CQ-Roll Call via Getty 
 The goal, the NAACP said in a news release, is to "help voters navigate ballot cure requirements and ensure every eligible vote is counted and certified."
 “Black voters in Mississippi did everything right. They registered, turned out, stood in line, and cast their ballots. Now the process has to do its part," national NAACP President Derrick Johnson said in a statement. "With margins this thin, this is what we mean when we say every vote counts. We’re working to ensure Black voters are heard and we won’t stop until their votes are certified.”
 A Democratic victory would be a stunning defeat for Republicans, who have held both of the state's Senate seats for decades.
 3d ago / 4:01 PM EST Rep. Jamie Raskin says he’ll investigate the Trump administration to ‘defend our system of government against authoritarians’ 
 Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, said today that anyone interested in his plans to investigate the Trump administration in the next Congress should "go back and read my letters."
 Graeme Sloan / Bloomberg via Getty 
 Raskin has sent more than 200 letters to the Justice Department and the White House seeking to document corruption in the administration. 
 "It’s a pretty good trail of crumbs of what we’re going to do, because, like, this is not a game of surprise or gotcha," he said at an event held by the Center for American Progress. "We’re talking about trying to defend our system of government against authoritarians here.”
 With Democrats set to take control of both chambers of Congress, Raskin plans to “enforce the law” over the administration spending taxpayer dollars on “political propaganda,” seeming to refer to Trump’s TV ads aimed at boosting MAGA support for him and the Republican Party. 
 Show more Democrats on the Judiciary Committee, including Raskin, have announced they plan to investigate presidential pardons for MAGA loyalists and foreign governments' buying influence through payments to the Trump family . 
 Since Democrats have been in the minority the past four years, they did not have the votes to issue subpoenas or schedule oversight hearings, which will change come January. 
 3d ago / 3:55 PM EST There’s a new political party in Indiana 
 Indiana has a new political party: the Lincoln Party.
 The party's first candidate, former two-term Indianapolis Mayor Greg Ballard, won more than 3% of the vote in the Indiana secretary of state's race Tuesday, according to initial results . Under state law, if a candidate wins at least 2% of the vote in that race, his or her party secures ballot access for the next four years.
 “We got the party started!” Ballard said today in a phone interview.
 The Lincoln Party does not have a strict policy platform, though it does have a list of principles. 
 “We got asked this all through the campaign — ‘what’s the platform? what do you stand for?’” Ballard said in the interview. “I said, 'We’re not worried about that, because it’s not like either party follows their own platform anyway!'”
 Show more Ballard said that his campaign manager, Nathan Gotsch, will oversee the party and that they plan to start building a statewide infrastructure and recruiting candidates for next year's municipal races.
 “We’re not gonna try to flood the zone, we’re not gonna try and get candidates in every race throughout — we’re gonna go slowly and make sure we have a good reputation for putting forth good candidates,” Ballard said.
 He went on to say he sees an opportunity for his nascent party in the Democratic blue wave that swept across the country in Tuesday's midterm elections.
 "A lot of folks seem to think that the Republicans came out to vote, but they voted for the Democrats. So this may be an opportunity to make people think about the parties differently," he said. "I think we have an opportunity here with what just happened to get our message out a little bit more forcefully than in just a normal year."
 3d ago / 3:51 PM EST Gina Hinojosa pledges to work with Republicans to be a 'governor for all the people of Texas' 
 Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa emphasized her commitment to leading with bipartisanship today, telling reporters, "This is not about being a Democratic administration." 
 Mikala Compton / Austin American-Statesman via Getty 
 "This is about my campaign promises, what I ran to create as governor. We are forging a new way forward. People are tired of the divisions, of the fighting, tired of the culture wars," Hinojosa said at a news conference. "I'm not going to be the governor for just Democrats. I'm going to be the governor for all the people of Texas." 
 Hinojosa appeared with several officials who she said will be helping with the transition to her administration, including Ernest Bailes, a former Republican state representative. 
 Hinojosa said that Bailes is "a champion for public schools" and that his work in the administration shows her "commitment for this to be a transition that truly represents all of Texas." 
 Show more "There is really little light between our positions on public education, and as such, he serves as a tremendous leader on this transition team," said Hinojosa, who made education a pillar of her campaign . "There are lots of issues with whom my good allies are Republicans. So I'm just about delivering for people." 
 Hinojosa also said she hopes that "elected leaders from both parties don’t get in the way of the progress we can make together to deliver for working people." 
 Her early commitment to work across the aisle comes as Democratic Senate-elect James Talarico has also pledged to work with Trump and Republicans in Washington to best represent the people in Texas. 
 3d ago / 3:42 PM EST California Gov. Gavin Newsom commutes all death sentences 
 Gov. Gavin Newsom commuted all California death sentences today, declaring that “state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with” values in America’s most populous state.
 Tayfun Cokun / Anadolu via Getty 
 In an open letter to constituents, Newsom said taking that step is “among the most difficult of my career.”
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 3:26 PM EST How anger helped fuel Latino voter turnout and a historic Democratic shift in Texas 
 Texas developer Mario Guerrero had sounded the alarm earlier this year that Trump’s worksite raids in the Rio Grande Valley would cost the Republican Party. But the raids at border businesses didn’t stop.
 People celebrate as Gina Hinojosa is announced as the next governor of Texas at her watch party in Austin on Tuesday.   Mikala Compton / Austin American-Statesman via Getty 
 “Everyone was mad,” said Guerrero, executive director of the South Texas Builders Association, who voted for Trump three times.
 So, as he sees it, the Republicans’ Election Day rout in Texas was “karma coming back full circle.”
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 3:21 PM EST Democrat JoAnna Mendoza wins Arizona's 6th Congressional District, NBC News projects 
 Democrat JoAnna Mendoza has defeated Republican Juan Ciscomani to win Arizona's 6th Congressional District, NBC News projects.
 See the latest results here. 
 3d ago / 2:49 PM EST Trump’s D.C.-area arch expected to be approved, but without sniper or drone plan 
 The National Capital Planning Commission is expected to approve Trump’s massive — and controversial — “ Triumphal Arch ” for Washington, D.C., today, with construction scheduled to begin almost immediately.
 President Donald Trump holds up a model of his proposed arch at the White House last year.   Demetrius Freeman / Washington Post via Getty 
 The commission, led by Trump appointees, is considered likely to give the project a green light after a hearing at which numerous area residents lined up to voice their opposition to the project, which would sit in Memorial Circle between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 2:06 PM EST Justice Department moves to toss Steve Bannon’s conviction tied to Congress’ Jan. 6 investigation 
 The Trump administration moved today to vacate the conviction of Steve Bannon on two counts of contempt of Congress in connection with its investigation into the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol.
 Shelby Tauber / Bloomberg via Getty 
 Bannon, a White House chief strategist and senior counselor during Trump’s first term, served a four-month prison sentence after the conviction in 2022.
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 2:02 PM EST Scott Colom criticizes Democrats for writing off Mississippi amid close Senate vote count 
 Democrat Scott Colom criticized his party for writing off Mississippi as he remains locked in a Senate race that is too close to call, telling NBC News that Democrats unfairly gave up on voters in the state.
 Sarah Warnock / AP 
 “Let’s not give them too much credit. They haven’t been trying, right?” Colom, a local prosecutor, said of national Democrats, who are excited about the prospect of winning a Senate seat in Mississippi for the first time since 1982. “I’ve been in Mississippi [for] 15 years. Most of the time, the Democrats conceded the state.”
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 1:45 PM EST Head of DOJ Civil Rights Division resigns after GOP midterms loss 
 Harmeet Dhillon, the Republican attorney who oversaw a massive overhaul of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, submitted her resignation today.
 David Crane / Los Angeles Daily News via Getty 
 Attorney General Todd Blanche posted on X that he has accepted Dhillon’s resignation. He wrote that she “defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor” and that the DOJ “is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors.”
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 1:08 PM EST Gronk bonks Election Day criticism after appearance outside N.H. polling place 
 Patriots great Rob Gronkowski took to social media today to push back against claims he took a political stance in an appearance outside a New Hampshire polling place on Election Day.
 Gronkowski and his girlfriend Camille Kostek met with Gov. Kelly Ayotte at polling location in New Hampshire on Tuesday.   NBC10 Boston 
 The former NFL tight end, who's being inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame this weekend, was photographed near a Turning Point USA tent and seen on video chatting with Republican officials, including Gov. Kelly Ayotte, who won re-election later that night.
 The interactions led to online criticism and a Daily Beast headline that said he "outs himself as MAGA." 
 In a post on Instagram , Gronkowski, who's known as "Gronk," said it's been "upsetting and eye opening to see the narratives around my visit." 
 Show more The former football star said he's "not endorsed by or affiliated with Turning Point USA," and that he and girlfriend Camille Kostek had been at a nearby high school when fans yelled them over to the location. 
 "We took photos with people across the political spectrum throughout that morning," he wrote. 
 "It's disappointing to see an innocent moment stripped of context and turned into clickbait," he said in the post. "Our message has always been and always will be to treat everyone with kindness and hope you all will do the same."
 3d ago / 12:56 PM EST California rejects Proposition 39: Require voter ID, NBC News projects 
 California voters have rejected Proposition 39: Require voter ID, NBC News projects.
 See the latest results here. 
 3d ago / 12:56 PM EST Schumer delivers warning for Trump if he vetoes 'common sense legislation' 
 During a speech this morning, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., warned that the 2028 elections will be grim for Republicans if Trump blocks Democrats' legislative efforts to lower costs, root out corruption and end chaos. 
 "If Donald Trump does spend the next year vetoing common sense legislation to lower costs and end corruption, this election, this absolute Republican catastrophe on election night 2026, will look like a good day compared to what will come down on Republicans in the 2028 election," Schumer said at an event held by the Center for American Progress.
 Schumer said that one reason Democrats were successful is because they were able to zero in their messaging on costs, chaos and corruption. He also praised the slate of Democratic candidates and explained that his party set out early to recruit potential candidates early in the cycle and across the country.
 He also argued that there was a false binary between populism and moderation. He said that creating a durable majority requires a big tent that includes people with different perspectives. 
 3d ago / 12:47 PM EST Democratic socialist Nithya Raman defeats Karen Bass in the Los Angeles mayor’s race 
 City Council member Nithya Raman has defeated incumbent Karen Bass in the Los Angeles mayoral race, NBC News projects, capping off a rapid political ascent for a progressive challenger who railed against the “broken status quo” in the country’s second-largest metropolis.
 Jackson Tammariello / Zuma via Reuters 
 Raman, 45, who is part of the Democratic Socialists of America, unseated Bass, a former six-term congresswoman and a fixture of California’s political scene for decades. The result means three major cities will be led by democratic socialists, with Raman joining New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Janeese Lewis George , who won the mayor’s race in Washington, D.C. this week.
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 12:45 PM EST Nithya Raman wins Los Angeles race for mayor 
 NBC News projects that Nithya Raman has won the Los Angeles, California, race for mayor, beating incumbent Karen Bass.
 See the latest results here. 
 3d ago / 12:44 PM EST California Rep. Pete Aguilar running for House Majority Whip 
 Rep. Pete Aguilar of California, the current chair of the House Democratic Caucus, is running to be the majority whip next Congress, he announced to his colleagues in a letter today.
 Bill Clark / CQ-Roll Call via Getty 
 If he’s successful, this would mean Aguilar would continue being the third most powerful House Democrat, behind Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York (who is seeking the speakership) and Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts (who is running for majority leader). 
 “With a Democratic majority, we’ll have the tools to rein in this out-of-control administration and investigate the agencies, officials and corporations that have been making life harder and more expensive for our communities,” Aguilar wrote in the letter. “I look forward to working with each of you to deliver on our affordability agenda.”
 Aguilar is the highest-ranking Latino in House history. He was first elected to the House in 2014. 
 3d ago / 12:30 PM EST Tech stocks plunge on worries about AI and Democrats’ midterm landslide 
 Shares in technology companies dropped sharply today, compounding recent declines and sparking concerns about the durability of an artificial intelligence boom that has driven much of recent U.S. economic growth.
 The tech-focused Nasdaq 100 index dropped more than 6% in midmorning trading, to its lowest level in five months.
 The S&P 500 also fell 3.5%, putting it on track for its worst day since April 2025, when Trump’s global tariffs rocked markets. The S&P 500’s drop erased nearly $2.5 trillion in wealth from the index.
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 11:50 AM EST Democrat Amish Shah wins Arizona's 1st Congressional District, NBC News projects 
 Democrat Amish Shah has defeated Republican Jay Feely to win Arizona's 1st Congressional District, NBC News projects.
 See the latest results here. 
 3d ago / 11:29 AM EST Rep. Ro Khanna allies launch a draft campaign for the 2028 presidential race 
 Rep. Ro Khanna’s allies are launching an effort to lay the groundwork for the California Democrat to run for president, the leaders of a new draft committee told NBC News.
 Jason Henry / Bloomberg via Getty 
 Former Rep. Jamaal Bowman, D-N.Y., and progressive strategist Nomiki Konst are serving as co-chairs of the group — “Run Ro” — which can raise money from donors and begin building support for a Khanna candidacy while he continues to weigh a 2028 bid.
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 10:39 AM EST Rep. Thomas Massie says he'll try again to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth 
 Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., said he will reintroduce articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Congress returns next week. 
 “There is one contingency in which I won’t reintroduce the articles of impeachment: Hegseth resigns,” Massie posted on X last night. He has repeatedly criticized Trump, Hegseth and Republican leaders in Congress for their support of the Iran war. 
 Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky.   Tom Williams / CQ-Roll Call via Getty 
 Massie also warned this morning that his “Hegseth impeachment resolution is a much gentler version of what’s coming when Dem’s control Congress,” adding that Democrats would “have hearings & trials.” 
 Massie had attempted to force a vote on impeaching Hegseth in September, but Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., sent the House home early before that vote had to be held. 
 Show more “It’s a publicity stunt by someone who wants attention,” Johnson said in September of the impeachment push. “It will immediately be tabled, of course. ... We’ll probably do it when we come back, but it’s a stunt.” 
 The House returns to Washington on Monday, Nov. Massie would have to introduce his impeachment resolution as privileged to force a vote next week. 
 He would need several Republicans to join with all Democrats in supporting the measure for it to be successful. 
 NBC News will be reaching out to House Republicans to see if any will support Massie’s renewed impeachment attempt. 
 3d ago / 10:37 AM EST Inside the miscalculations that cost Trump control of Congress 
 In late August, Trump’s top advisers gathered at Camp David, the wooded sanctuary in Maryland where presidents seclude themselves to plot war plans, cut deals or play golf. Trump’s team was there, without him, to devise a strategy for the midterms — if not to win, at least to limit the damage.
 They didn’t have much to work with.
 The president’s party almost always loses ground in midterms, and Trump’s record offered few promising angles for reversing that curse.
 Read the full story here. 
 3d ago / 9:28 AM EST Planning commission to vote on Trump's arch 
 The National Capital Planning Commission is expected to vote today on whether to give Trump's so-called “Triumphal Arch” final approval.
 The president is planning to build the arch across the Potomac River from D.C., near Arlington National Cemetery. The plans have been highly controversial and prompted legal challenges. In recent days, the governments of both D.C. and Virginia have sued over the planned construction.

 3d ago / 8:59 AM EST After election rout, Trump says 'no other fair solution' than to hand Sen. Sullivan his opponents' votes 
 Trump said in a Truth Social post this morning that the votes for challenger candidate Dan Sullivan should be given to incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan in the Alaska Senate race, which remains too early to call. 
 "The vote totals for the Fake Dan Sullivan, plus the other 'slug' that the Dems put on the Ballot, should be immediately given to the REAL Dan Sullivan, and the Election is over — He easily wins," Trump said in the post. "There is no other fair solution!"
 This could ultimately happen through Alaska's ranked choice voting system.
 Under Alaska's election system, if none of the four candidates receive a majority of votes on the first ballot, election officials hold an instant runoff race based on how voters rank the four candidates. The candidate with the fewest votes is cut, and voters who listed that candidate as their top choice will have their votes distributed to the candidate they list as their second choice.
 This means that challenger Dan Sullivan's votes could ultimately be distributed to incumbent Dan Sullivan regardless, depending on how voters rank the candidates.
